catalog_quote: Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length) Stress is usually on the first syllable of two-syllable words. Syllables with long vowels always have stress. ... Conventions: Phonological ... /r/ is pronounced [d] word medially following homorganic nasal in unstressed syllables.

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: both deciding sentences and the supporting allophone note are verbatim on p. 3 of the held, at the stated section headings. (2) Deciding source: a 4-page SIL Organised Phonology Data sheet (Lindrud, data 1992, printed 2004) — a summary form, not a grammar or phonology paper; its stress content is two sentences. Glottolog 5.1 lists no published grammar/phonology for Kol; the only phonology is Lindrud's unpublished 44-pp 'Preliminary Kol phonology' ms (the OPD's own cited source), held privately by Hammarström with no open copy.org/OLAC/Wayback were unreachable, so the negative is bounded by Glottolog's 16-item list. (3) fetched sources now: Dunn, Reesink & Terrill 2002 (open, MPG PuRe) — silent on stress. Wishlist is headed by the Lindrud ms (archive-only); Stebbins et al. 2018 (paywalled DOI) and Lindrud
